extracted.intended_audience: compliance officers, legal counsel, and regulatory staff at covered financial institutions (banks, broker-dealers) and FinCEN/OMB reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Federal Register notice renewing the OMB control number for 31 CFR 1010.630 (prohibition on correspondent accounts for foreign shell banks and related recordkeeping), including definitions of covered entities, exemptions, procedural requirements (certification/recertification/verification/closure), and assignment of PRA burden hours and estimation methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'covered financial institution'
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'covered financial institution,' as defined for purposes of 31 CFR 1010.630, is comprised of entities subject to the AML program requirements for banks at 31 CFR 1020.210 plus the entities subject to the AML program requirements for brokers or dealers in securities at 31 CFR 1023.210.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FinCEN counts entities subject to those AML program requirements when estimating respondents; the definition aggregates multiple legal entity labels under the single concept of a covered financial institution for burden calculation purposes. See 31 CFR 1010.100(d) for related definitions and statutory background.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on correspondent accounts for foreign shell banks (31 CFR 1010.630(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: 31 CFR 1010.630(a)(1) prohibits a covered financial institution from establishing, maintaining, administering, or managing an account in the United States for, or on behalf of, a foreign shell bank. It also requires reasonable steps to ensure that accounts established, maintained, administered or managed for a foreign bank are not used to provide services to foreign shell banks indirectly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FinCEN assigns an estimated incremental recordkeeping burden of one hour per foreign correspondent account per year for (a)(1). Rationale: documenting an absence of an activity (not dealing with shell banks) is unlikely to generate lengthy documentation; many steps overlap with 31 CFR 1010.610 or other components of 1010.630 (particularly (c),(d),(e)), so burden is minimized to avoid double counting. Example: use of FinCEN's optional certification form to obtain assurances from foreign bank that it is not a shell bank.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain ownership and agent-for-service records (31 CFR 1010.630(a)(2)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires covered financial institutions to maintain, in the United States, for each foreign bank for which they maintain a correspondent account: (1) records that identify the owners of the foreign bank and (2) the name and address of an authorized agent who agrees to accept service of legal process for records and who resides in the United States. Partial exceptions apply (see (a)(2)(ii)-(iii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FinCEN assigns zero hours of incremental burden to this subsection because maintaining ownership and agent-for-service records is treated as a proper subset of the recordkeeping activities required by 31 CFR 1010.630(e) and would otherwise be double counted. FinCEN expects such records to be produced/maintained as part of other due diligence activities, and may be satisfied via the optional FinCEN certification form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions from ownership-record requirements (31 CFR 1010.630(a)(2)(ii) and (a)(2)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsections (a)(2)(ii) and (a)(2)(iii) define subpopulations of foreign banks for which a covered financial institution is not required to maintain ownership records: foreign banks that have filed Form FR Y-7 with the Federal Reserve and foreign banks whose shares are publicly traded on a market regulated by a foreign securities authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FinCEN assigns zero burden hours to these subsections. Rationale: exemptions reduce paperwork by minimizing duplication of information already reported to other authorities and avoid redundant recordkeeping. Exemptions are expected to reduce respondent burden materially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe harbor on recertification frequency (31 CFR 1010.630(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: 31 CFR 1010.630(b) establishes a safe harbor that, provided a covered financial institution continues to meet obligations under 31 CFR 1010.630(c) and (d), the institution need not obtain (re)certification of foreign banks for which it maintains correspondent accounts more than once every three years to satisfy 1010.630(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FinCEN assigns no hours of recordkeeping burden to (b). The safe harbor is expected to reduce paperwork and respondent burden because records/documentation evidencing satisfaction of the conditions should already be generated by activities required under (c) and (d) and other due diligence obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to verify or correct information (31 CFR 1010.630(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: 31 CFR 1010.630(c) requires a covered financial institution to request verification or correction of any information in a (re)certification if the institution knows, suspects, or has reason to suspect that information previously received is no longer correct, and to take appropriate measures to ascertain accuracy or obtain correct information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FinCEN currently assigns no incremental recordkeeping burden to this component under this OMB control number because much of the activity and associated records overlap with other due diligence obligations (e.g., 31 CFR 1010.610). FinCEN requests comments and data on the frequency and burden of interim verifications to assess this approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account-closure timing and accommodations (31 CFR 1010.630(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: 31 CFR 1010.630(d)(1) historically provided an accommodation granting covered financial institutions with accounts in existence as of October 28, 2002 additional time (154 calendar days) to bring such accounts into compliance, while newer accounts had 30 calendar days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FinCEN notes the accommodation is no longer expected to meaningfully reduce burden because affected accounts have been subject to the same requirements for over two decades. It therefore assigns no special burden relief in current estimates on that basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to obtain (re)certification/information to avoid account closure (31 CFR 1010.630(d)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: If requisite (re)certification or information cannot be obtained within required timeframes, correspondent accounts must be closed; foreign correspondent accounts established after Oct 28, 2002 must be closed within a commercially reasonable time and may not be used for new activity while closure occurs. The obligation to obtain information flows from the account-closure requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FinCEN assigns a recordkeeping time burden of two hours associated with activities necessary to obtain the (re)certification or required information needed to prevent account closure. Rationale: estimate reflects anticipated operationalization, incremental activities unique to 1010.630, and overlap with other due diligence obligations. FinCEN assumes the optional certification form will often be used and that foreign banks typically can provide the information without extensive incremental effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory account closure for nonresponsive foreign banks (31 CFR 1010.630(d)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: 31 CFR 1010.630(d)(3) requires a covered financial institution to close all correspondent accounts with any foreign bank that fails to provide verification or corrected information within 90 days of the covered financial institution's inquiry, and prohibits reestablishing accounts with that foreign bank.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FinCEN assigns no incremental recordkeeping burden to compliance with (d)(3) because records generated by closing an account or not opening new accounts are expected to be included in the records documenting broader due diligence activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on reestablishment until (re)certification received (31 CFR 1010.630(d)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a foreign correspondent account is closed due to inability to timely obtain (re)certification or necessary information, a covered financial institution may not reestablish the account or open new accounts with that foreign bank until the requisite (re)certification is received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FinCEN does not have separate data to estimate the number of (re)certifications pursued specifically for reestablishment; its aggregate estimate of approximately 177 (re)certifications per covered financial institution per year is intended to include such events. The associated burden per (re)certification is expected to average four hours (summation of components discussed elsewhere). FinCEN requests comment and data on frequency and burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on liability for account termination (31 CFR 1010.630(d)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: 31 CFR 1010.630(d)(5) limits the liability of a covered financial institution where termination of a correspondent account is executed in compliance with 1010.630(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This liability limitation is expected to reduce paperwork and compliance burden by lessening incentives for defensive over-documentation; FinCEN assigns zero incremental recordkeeping burden to this component.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping and retention obligations under 31 CFR 1010.630(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: 31 CFR 1010.630(e) encompasses record retention and maintenance of documentation associated with (re)certification, verification, and other related activities; FinCEN treats records required by (a)(2) as part of (e) for burden accounting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FinCEN assigns the recordkeeping burden for ownership records, agent-for-service records, and other documentation to subsection (e) to avoid double-counting. Prior estimates assigned time for maintaining records (e.g., 9 hours per institution); current renewals harmonize these assignments across related OMB control numbers. Where (e) overlaps with 31 CFR 1010.610 activities, FinCEN may attribute burden to the other OMB control number to avoid double counting.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRA burden hour assignments for certification, recertification, and recordkeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: FinCEN's current estimate assigns 20 hours to complete a certification for a foreign bank, five hours to complete a recertification for a foreign bank, and nine hours to maintain records on the foreign bank's (re)certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These estimates reflect the time to review instructions, search existing data sources, gather and maintain data, complete and review collections of information, and maintain records. FinCEN notes potential prior overestimation due to overlapping OMB control numbers and is harmonizing methodology across related renewals (e.g., OMB control number 1506-0046). Historical prior estimates (2018, 2022) used different aggregations (e.g., combined burdens summing to ~30 hours per institution); FinCEN explains reasons for changes and requests comment/data where uncertainty remains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology for estimating affected respondents and correspondent-account populations
rubrics_metrics.description: FinCEN estimates the distribution and counts of covered financial institutions and those expected to maintain correspondent accounts using public datasets (FDIC quarterly data, NCUA quarterly summaries, Board of Governors Master Account and Services Database, FR Y-7 filings, SEC data on active broker-dealers, Call Reports and UBPRs) and conservative assumptions (e.g., estimated 0.8% of broker-dealers maintain foreign correspondent accounts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FinCEN explains how it derives the total potential respondents (e.g., 12,637 covered financial institutions) and the expected respondents that maintain correspondent accounts (approx. 104 institutions). The methodology rationale, data sources, cohort assumptions, and conservative adjustments (e.g., treating non-public broker-dealers similarly to banks) are documented to increase transparency and to support burden calculations; FinCEN requests comment on these assumptions and any alternative data.
